sections.headline: Nvidia Earnings Spark Market Sell-Off
sections.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.1% to 7335.06 as traders sold off Nvidia's stock ahead of its earnings report, which is expected to provide insight into the AI trade. The decline in Nvidia's stock was accompanied by a broader market sell-off, with the Dow and Nasdaq also falling. The market's reaction to Nvidia's earnings is being closely watched by traders, who are concerned about the health of the AI industry.

sections.headline: Nasdaq Falls Amid Tech Woes
sections.body: The Nasdaq fell 0.95% to 24276.52 as traders reacted to concerns over Nvidia's AI technology and US export restrictions on tech stocks. The decline in tech stocks was also influenced by a reported NSA network outage, which added to the uncertainty in the market. [8]

sections.headline: Treasury Yields Ease Amid Market Uncertainty
sections.body: The 10-year yield fell 0.31% to 5.11 as investors took a step back from the market, citing concerns over the AI market slump [9]. Retail sales data also came under scrutiny, leading to a moderate decline in Treasury yields [10]. Meanwhile, a report from Morningstar suggests that inflation is still a concern, but not enough to spark a significant increase in yields [11]. The decline in gold prices may also be contributing to the easing of Treasury yields, as a stronger dollar and rising yields make gold less attractive [12].

sections.headline: US Yields Spark Yen Buying
sections.body: Traders are watching the impact of falling US yields on the Japanese yen, which has led to increased buying pressure and a decline in the USD/JPY pair. The yen's value is also being influenced by concerns over potential Japanese intervention to support the currency. As a result, the USD/JPY fell to 159.31, as traders adjusted their positions in response to the changing market dynamics.

sections.headline: Middle East Tensions Boost Oil Prices
sections.body: Oil prices rebounded due to ongoing tensions in the Middle East, which has been a concern for traders. The WSJ reported that oil prices are caught between tanker attacks and rising Mideast exports, citing Reuters and CNBC. This suggests that traders are watching the situation closely, as it could impact oil supply and prices.

sections.headline: Gold's Late Rally
sections.body: Gold rose 0.13% to 3858.0 as traders took profits from the previous day's one-year low, citing a rebound in the US dollar and yields, which made gold less attractive. [23] Traders are also watching the gold market in India, where demand is expected to get a festive boost, but this move was not reflected in the global price. [24]

USD/JPY (-0.29% to 159.31): US Yields Spark Yen Buying. The yen's value is also being influenced by concerns over potential Japanese intervention to support the currency. As a result, the USD/JPY fell to 159.31, as traders adjusted their positions in response to the changing market dynamics.

The WSJ reported that oil prices are caught between tanker attacks and rising Mideast exports, citing Reuters and CNBC. This suggests that traders are watching the situation closely, as it could impact oil supply and prices.
Gold (+0.13% to 3858.0): Gold's Late Rally. Gold rose 0.13% to 3858.0 as traders took profits from the previous day's one-year low, citing a rebound in the US dollar and yields, which made gold less attractive.
